faq.a: Huseyin is associated with the Arabic form حُسَيْن, whose core sense is huseyin; diminutive of 'handsome' (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Huseyin?
faq.a: Huseyin is associated with Arabic. Huseyin is the Turkish form of Arabic حُسَيْن (Ḥusayn), a diminutive of حَسَن, meaning 'handsome, good'.
Yes — the underlying form حُسَيْن is Arabic.
Huseyin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Huseyin should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ḥusayn is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Huseyin mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Huseyin is rendered حسین and carries the sense حسین، نیکو.
A romanized syllable approximation is hu-seyin. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Huseyin, huseyin. Script forms are حسين, حسین, حُسَيْن, हुसैन.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
